name: evtx_query
description: Query an EVTX event log and return filtered events with timestamp, event id, channel, computer, provider, EventRecordID and named data fields. A run reports three counts apart: records_examined (every record the reader produced), events_matched (records that parsed and passed every filter) and parse_errors (records or chunk chains that could not be read, with their offsets); an error row is never counted as a match, and a run with any parse error, or whose chunks could not be enumerated to the end, is status partial. Every row carries record_offset, chunk_offset, the EventRecordID and record_filetime (the FILETIME in the record header, as a decimal string, with record_time_utc by integer arithmetic) beside the XML's own SystemTime. Filters: event_ids, contains (a substring of the XML), start_record and end_record, and start_time and end_time (ISO 8601 UTC prefixes compared with the XML's SystemTime). The XML of every match is kept in the result file (JSON Lines); limit is the inline page size. SENSITIVE: event data can hold command lines and text typed into one, which can hold a secret; run it as a job with secret_output: true when the log may.

event_ids.description: Optional list of numeric event IDs to include

contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring that must appear in the XML

limit.description: Events shown inline (default 200, an inline page size); every matching event and its whole XML is kept in result_file, and parse-error rows are listed under errors and kept there too

out_file.description: Optional JSONL result path under the run; defaults to a deterministic path under work/

start_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 UTC lower bound on the XML's SystemTime, as a prefix (2026-09-01 or 2026-09-01T10:00)

end_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 UTC upper bound on the XML's SystemTime, compared as a prefix: 2026-09-01 includes the whole day
